technical_and_design_decisions: Reuse the existing Spring XD module/plugin architecture for the new Reactor-based processor (U2) and follow the established pattern of Spark and RxJava processor plugins.
Implement the YARN info command (U1) by extending the existing xd-yarn shell script to query ZooKeeper for the admin container's address, rather than adding a new runtime component.
For message history (U3), implement a header-enriching tap/interceptor that is enabled via a stream/module option, leaving existing streams backward-compatible (opt-in).
The Protocol Buffers codec (U4) will be implemented as a pluggable codec that follows the existing CodecFactory SPI, supporting a user-supplied .proto schema descriptor or pre-generated Java classes.
Ambari plugin (U6) will be delivered as an Ambari service definition (metainfo.xml + scripts) plus a custom stack definition, reusing Spring XD's existing REST admin API for management and metrics.

For U7/U8, treat the existing JdbcHfsOptionsMetadata bean as the source of truth; surface clear validation error messages and align the wiki with the existing @AssertTrue logic (no behavior change beyond messaging clarity).
All features will be implemented by a single experienced Spring XD developer using Java 8 (consistent with the Spring XD era), with JUnit and integration tests covering each user story.
Use existing Spring XD build (Maven) and CI conventions; no new build infrastructure is introduced.
assumptions: Effort is expressed in person-workdays (1 workday = 8 productive hours) for a single experienced Spring XD developer.
The Spring XD codebase, build, and CI pipeline are already in place and understood by the developer (no ramp-up time is included beyond what is naturally embedded in each activity).
External dependencies (Apache ZooKeeper client, Reactor Core, Google Protobuf Java library, Ambari Python service framework) are already available or can be added with trivial pom changes.
Ambari plugin scripts will be delivered in Python following the standard Ambari Service Definition conventions; no custom Ambari server patches are required.
Protobuf codec supports the dynamic-schema use case via reflection on pre-compiled messages, since shipping a protoc compiler to end users is out of scope.
Documentation/wiki updates (U7) are done inline with the implementation activities; a separate 'final docs' activity captures the cross-story review and example updates.
Performance benchmarking in U5 is done with simple JMH-style harnesses embedded in integration tests, not a full benchmarking deliverable.
No production hardening, security review, or release engineering effort is included beyond basic tests and docs.

activities.activity_description: Extend the xd-yarn shell script with an 'info' subcommand that connects to the configured ZooKeeper ensemble, looks up the XD admin container's published address/port, and prints it. Includes parsing the existing xd-yarn config, ZK path conventions, and basic shell tests.

Design and implement a new reactor-based stream processor plugin module that mirrors the Spark/RxJava processor plugins: bare-minimum module metadata (processor class) plus extension points for options, and a sample processor used to validate the design.

Introduce a 'history' (or 'messageHistoryHeader') module option that, when enabled, injects stream name, module name, module type and timestamp into the message header as it traverses taps/processors. Includes the header propagation logic, configuration plumbing, and tests.

Implement a ProtobufCodec implementing the Spring XD Codec interface, plug it into the existing CodecFactory, and provide module option support for specifying the message type or descriptor. Includes serialization/deserialization logic, option metadata, and unit tests.
